audit_status.source_base: ChatGPT-authored Psalms completion draft using public-domain KJV as familiar alignment scaffold with curated Hebrew/textual overrides; full WLC/OSHB/source-witness audit pending
audit_status.review_note: Shepherd imagery, rest, deep darkness, enemies, anointing, abundance, and dwelling.

verses.restored: The YHWH is my shepherd; I shall not want.

familiar.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.

modern.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.

original.text: מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִ֑ד יְהוָ֥ה רֹ֝עִ֗י לֹ֣א אֶחְסָֽר

verses.restored: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.

familiar.text: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.

modern.text: He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters.

original.text: בִּנְא֣וֹת דֶּ֭שֶׁא יַרְבִּיצֵ֑נִי עַל מֵ֖י מְנֻח֣וֹת יְנַהֲלֵֽנִי

verses.restored: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

familiar.text: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

modern.text: He restores my soul; He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.

original.text: נַפְשִׁ֥י יְשׁוֹבֵ֑ב יַֽנְחֵ֥נִי בְמַעְגְּלֵי צֶ֝֗דֶק לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֽוֹ

verses.restored: Even though I walk through a valley of deep darkness, I fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff comfort me.

familiar.text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

notes.title: Tsalmavet
notes.body: The Hebrew tsalmavet is traditionally “shadow of death” but is widely understood as “deep darkness” or “gloom.” The restored text uses “deep darkness” while retaining the traditional reading in comparison layers.

modern.text: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.

original.text: גַּ֤ם כִּֽי אֵלֵ֨ךְ בְּגֵ֪יא צַלְמָ֡וֶת לֹא אִ֘ירָ֤א רָ֗ע כִּי אַתָּ֥ה עִמָּדִ֑י שִׁבְטְךָ֥ וּ֝מִשְׁעַנְתֶּ֗ךָ הֵ֣מָּה יְנַֽחֲמֻֽנִי

verses.restored: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.

familiar.text: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.

modern.text: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.

original.text: תַּעֲרֹ֬ךְ לְפָנַ֨י שֻׁלְחָ֗ן נֶ֥גֶד צֹרְרָ֑י דִּשַּׁ֖נְתָּ בַשֶּׁ֥מֶן רֹ֝אשִׁ֗י כּוֹסִ֥י רְוָיָֽה

verses.restored: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the YHWH for ever.

familiar.text: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

modern.text: Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever.

original.text: אַ֤ךְ ט֤וֹב וָחֶ֣סֶד יִ֭רְדְּפוּנִי כָּל יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֑י וְשַׁבְתִּ֥י בְּבֵית יְ֝הוָ֗ה לְאֹ֣רֶךְ יָמִֽים

translation_notes: This chapter expands corpus coverage while remaining explicitly pending a deeper Hebrew/source-witness audit. KJV is retained only as the familiar comparison layer.

The completion draft intentionally preserves coherent traditional English syntax where a verse has not yet received a curated Hebrew-sensitive rendering; it does not mix archaic and modern grammar. Major identified lexical/textual issues receive explicit overrides and notes.
safety_note: Comfort poetry is not a promise that faithful people will avoid danger, illness, grief, or death.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Scrolls where extant, and other relevant witnesses during the global audit.
Preserve Psalm numbering and superscription differences across Hebrew and Greek traditions rather than silently harmonizing them.
